CARES PostgreSQL Logical ERD (Round 1)

Status: Logical ERD documented; NOT IMPLEMENTED, NOT TESTED. Mermaid diagrams represent proposed logical relationships only (no PostgreSQL DDL, indexes, policies, triggers, or implementation syntax). Entity definitions, cardinalities, and constraints must be read together with POSTGRESQL_LOGICAL_DATA_MODEL.md.

ERD conventions and limitations

  • Diagrams use Mermaid erDiagram syntax and focus on key entities/relationships for readability; not every attribute is shown.
  • Relationship labels indicate logical nature; optionality/cardinality details are normative in the entity catalogue and relationship analysis.
  • asset_data_source ↔ source_device_key_id/dependent source_device_key projection: Round 1.1 recommendation (Proposed, not approved; OD-002 open) is authoritative asset_data_source owning immutable stable binding identity with 1:1 dependent/non-authoritative projection only if materialized; diagrams show this recommended association and must not be read as approved physical design.
  • Tenant scoping is implied for tenant-owned entities; physical tenant-inclusive FK enforcement and RLS are future design concerns (not shown as SQL).
  • Global reference entities (e.g. shared threat intelligence catalog) are included only where needed to clarify boundaries.

Explanation (how multiple sources do not create duplicate licensed assets): One canonical ASSET (one unique monitored device, one licensed asset) may have many ASSET_DATA_SOURCE bindings, each representing a distinct reporting DATA_SOURCE device context. Each authoritative binding owns a stable binding identity (source_device_key_id, with any separate SOURCE_DEVICE_KEY record modeled only as a 1:1 dependent projection, Proposed) and may have one-or-more versioned SOURCE_DEVICE_FINGERPRINT_ALIAS records for lookup/rotation (aliases may overlap temporarily but resolve to the same stable binding identity/asset). ASSET_IDENTITY_CLAIM records preserve provenance and drive deterministic resolution or IDENTITY_RESOLUTION_CASE without auto-merge on ambiguity. License/accounting effects are represented through TENANT_LICENSE_USAGE_STATE, ASSET_LICENSE_EVENT, optional ASSET_LICENSE_RESERVATION, and IDENTITY_OPERATION_IDEMPOTENCY_LEDGER so retries/conflicts do not duplicate assets, bindings, or licensed usage. Merge/split operations preserve lineage and canonical ID non-reuse through typed, relationally enforceable lineage associations (no generic polymorphic asset/operation reference).

Explanation: EVENT_RECEIPT provides ingestion idempotency/acceptance truth with explicit deduplication namespace/provenance (tenant + namespace type/id + normalized source event key), separate from time-partitioned SECURITY_EVENT storage (physical partitioning deferred). OUTBOX_MESSAGE/OUTBOX_ATTEMPT model asynchronous processing and delivery ambiguity/replay metadata. AUDIT_EVENT (operational/security) is distinct from forensic evidence metadata (FORENSIC_EVIDENCE_RECORD), immutable object/version references (EVIDENCE_OBJECT_VERSION), and append-only custody history (EVIDENCE_CUSTODY_EVENT), with optional controlled transition authorization.

Explanation: Global identity (EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_SUBJECT) is separated from tenant-scoped access (TENANT_MEMBERSHIP, role assignments). SUPPORT_ACCESS_GRANT (and optional approval) models explicitly scoped, time-bound, auditable support access—never blanket cross-tenant access. Tenant-owned records (examples shown: asset, event, audit, configuration, AI config) require access only under verified transaction-bound tenant context and application authorization; PostgreSQL RLS is a future defense-in-depth control (not depicted as SQL). Role/permission granularity is proposed/assumption-level where not fully specified.

Intentionally omitted or simplified in ERDs

The following catalogue entities are intentionally not drawn in every ERD (or are simplified) to preserve readability; they remain part of the authoritative logical catalogue and must be considered in cross-document consistency:

  • AI_INTERACTION_AUDIT — specialized AI audit record, distinct from and correlatable/cross-referenced with AUDIT_EVENT.
  • PROCESSING_WORK_ITEM — optional/non-core pipeline work item; intentionally not a competing source of truth with event_receipt/outbox_message.
  • AI_PROVIDER_POLICY_CONSENT_REFERENCE, AI_PROVIDER_SECRET_REFERENCE, AI_USAGE_BUDGET_ACCOUNTING — AI configuration/policy/consent/budget references represented conceptually (ERD 4 shows tenant AI provider configuration context).
  • DETECTION_RULE, DETECTION_RULE_VERSION, INTEGRATION_CONFIGURATION, THREAT_INTELLIGENCE_REFERENCE — detection/integration/reference catalogue entities.
  • ASSET_INVENTORY_OBSERVATION — supporting observation records; core identity/licensing flow is represented via bindings/claims/ledger/assets.
  • Some RBAC/evidence/support detail multiplicities and optional workflow entities are simplified; the logical data model remains authoritative.

Assumptions and limitations

  • ERDs are intentionally simplified logical views; authoritative entity definitions, invariants, and full relationship analysis are in POSTGRESQL_LOGICAL_DATA_MODEL.md.
  • Some entities are represented by simplified names in diagrams (e.g. membership/assignment tables) to keep Mermaid readable; logical intent is unchanged.
  • Physical concerns intentionally omitted: SQL types, nullability DDL, indexes, partitioning, RLS policies, grants, triggers, functions, sequences, and migration artifacts.
  • Binding ownership recommendation is documented (Proposed, OD-002 requires approval). Reservation accounting, approval workflows, outbox attempt/lease-fencing details, and connector-specific dedup namespace fallback behavior remain Proposed or Open Decision and may block parts of Round 2 physical design.
